answer: Interleaved admission windows. Each new identity may submit its first action only inside a slot derived from a shared crystal clock, so a batch of agents must stagger across windows. A client whose action lands outside its assigned ledge of time is rejected, and the queue forces one live round-trip per window. Faking a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand sequential waits plus a sable margin of idle capacity held open per slot, making mass registration pay in elapsed time rather than fees.
